# Shared business staff authority — initial implementation contract

12 November 2026. Draft for two independent nonauthor Spec and Standards reviews before source edits. Baseline authority sources are bound below at focus df8fd4ef00cb9d45d081ce760d15cef84a880c4e; unrelated later edits do not change these bindings. Root owns integration. This contract follows SYSTEM_DESIGN sections 4–6, the domain glossary and the delegated pharmacy policy. It introduces one reusable authority boundary for pharmacy and lab staff, not a new login, general RBAC engine, organization migration or clinical workflow.

## Outcome and exact initial slice

Implement one usable internal resolver that turns an authenticated individual plus a requested business/branch/capability into a current, narrowly scoped BusinessScope, or denies. Implement its persistence shapes, restricted read adapter and framework-free eligibility rules. Valid synthetic facts must produce the expected scope; missing/invalid facts must deny. The initial source slice exposes no HTTP route, grant/verification writer, bootstrap command, index migration, clinical command, protected-data reader or payment/stock effect. It does not silently enable existing routes or promote existing business/admin tokens.

New production files only:

| File under src1/modules/organizations | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| types/index.ts | Closed capability/purpose and record types; readonly authority facts, lookup and scope; narrow read-port interface. No Express/Mongoose/typedi dependency. |
| rules.ts | Pure validation/evaluation of supplied facts and server time, including all cross-record/proof/version checks below; no database, environment, configuration, provider or logger access. |
| model/index.ts | Four explicitly named Mongoose schemas/models below, with strict fields and index declarations; no startup index creation/synchronization or data seeding. |
| repository/index.ts | The sole Mongo authority adapter and the explicit narrow projection adapters for existing User and Pharmacy facts. No inheritance from unscoped BaseRepository; no arbitrary caller filter/update/model exposure. |
| services/index.ts | Constructor-injected read port; validate caller context, obtain current facts within the caller's transaction, invoke the one rule evaluator and mint/freeze the internal scope. No default permissive port or singleton environment switch. |

No root dependency/lock/build/start, existing auth/user/pharmacy/admin source or routes change. Source QA may contain exact diff/hashes and review records. Meaningful pure-rule/port tests may be added to a separately reviewed focused test entry; do not add a redundant lexical-test framework, copy production controllers or run application imports under this contract.

## Identity and scope

- Reuse existing personal User._id, authenticated by the existing signature-verifying middleware, with userType exactly user. The resolver takes only an internal authenticated-principal projection, not a body/header token decoder. Reload the User by exact ID; require stored userType=user and isActive=true. Missing/false/unknown state denies. User.isVerified/otpVerified and linkedPharmacyId never establish professional or staff authority.
- A pharmacy token identifies a business, not a person. Reject pharmacy/admin/hr/specialist tokens for this resolver, including an admin with self-edited permissions. An individual may have customer and staff roles, but each invocation explicitly uses purpose=staff; do not union patient/dependent/caregiver rights or infer consent.
- Canonical organizationId is a new organization record ID. Initial mapping kind is pharmacy or lab; legacy business IDs remain separate references. Do not copy pharmacyId/corporateId into organizationId or invent an organization for an API provider. Branch IDs are explicit embedded organization branches; no implicit branch, wildcard, omitted branch or all-branches capability.
- Input contains exactly requested organizationId, branchId and one supported capability. Initial closed capabilities are pharmacy.prescription.review and lab.report.release. The first requires profession=pharmacist; the second requires profession=lab_signatory. A capability grants only the named action in this scope, never finance, catalogue, stock quality, exports, contact changes or professional verification.
- All IDs must be canonical lowercase 24-hex strings, with no coercion from objects, whitespace or numbers. Versions are positive safe integers; digests are lowercase 64-hex SHA-256. Arrays are bounded (at most 100 branches/grants), have unique keys and no unknown capability/branch/profession values. Reject malformed stored records as well as malformed input; Mongoose casting is not the validator.

The initial real business adapter supports only pharmacy. It reloads exact Pharmacy._id from the canonical organization mapping and requires isActive=true, isVerified=true and absent archivedAt. It checks that the protected mapping's source-field fingerprint still matches the current license number/document reference; business verification alone is insufficient. A changed or absent fingerprint denies even if the legacy verified flag remains true. The fingerprint detects changed fields, not overwritten remote URL bytes; immutable verification evidence is separately required. Lab always denies with AUTHORITY_MAPPING_UNAVAILABLE until its actual canonical business/branch adapter is separately contracted and reviewed. Lab types and capability use the same resolver; no fake lab ID or permissive placeholder adapter.

## Minimal persisted authority records

Use these four collections only. They contain authority/provenance references, not patient records, prescription/report content, credentials, document URLs or authentication secrets. IDs are immutable; createdAt/updatedAt are UTC. No public generic CRUD or direct model access outside the approved adapter. Every current record has schemaVersion=1 and positive revision, incremented by future protected writers; unknown versions deny.

| Collection | Required fields and invariant |
| --- | --- |
| business_authority_organizations | _id, kind, sourceBusinessId, state=active/suspended/revoked, revision, sourceFingerprint, mappingDecisionId, bounded branches[{branchId,state,revision}]. Exactly one organization per kind+sourceBusinessId, each branch belongs to that organization. No source/mapping/branch replacement through a profile update. |
| business_staff_memberships | _id, organizationId, actorId, state=active/suspended/revoked, revision, validFrom, expiresAt, and bounded grants[{branchId,capability,grantDecisionId}]. Exactly one current membership per organization+actor, retaining revoked rows. A grant is branch-specific and names a protected decision; capability arrays alone are not provenance. |
| business_professional_eligibility | _id, organizationId, actorId, profession, state=verified/suspended/revoked, revision, validFrom, expiresAt, verificationDecisionId, evidenceVersionId and evidenceSha256. One current record per organization+actor+profession. This is current verified eligibility, not a copied user/business flag; the referenced professional decision supplies the permitted branch/capability scope. History is retained in immutable decision records. |
| business_authority_decisions | _id, organizationId, operationId, decisionKind=business_mapped/membership_granted/professional_verified, subjectActorId where relevant, decidingActorId, decidedAt, authorityGeneration, schemaVersion=1, payloadSha256, exact payload and immutable evidence references. No update/delete methods. Payloads bind the exact relevant organization/source fingerprint, branch/grant, subject, record revision, profession and credential evidence versions/validity. Unknown kinds or mismatches deny. |

The resolver checks mapping, grant and professional decisions against the current records, not just that a decision ID exists. A grant/verification decidingActorId must differ from its subjectActorId. Membership-grant and professional-verification are distinct decision kinds; neither implies the other. A decision records the authority and evidence at decision time; a later verifier-role change does not silently rewrite history. Revoking current eligibility/membership or invalidating evidence blocks current use.

Decision authenticity originates in the separately protected grant/bootstrap path, not a client-supplied document or database label. A read-only readiness port supplies the accepted authorityGeneration and verified index/provenance readiness from trusted composition; it is not request input, an environment boolean or an editable Admin field. It defaults closed. All three decisions must match that accepted generation. Initial source supplies no way to activate it or fabricate records. No existing app/admin/profile writer may mint these records. Threats from privileged database tampering and restore rollback require the existing security/restore controls; schema immutability alone is not advertised as cryptographic or operational authenticity.

Use a fixed schema-versioned array serialization for each decision kind before SHA-256: explicit ordered field names/values, canonical IDs, integer revisions/epoch-millisecond times, sorted unique branch/capability entries and exact evidence digests. Do not hash arbitrary object iteration order, omit absent-vs-null distinctions or accept a submitted digest without recomputing it. The exact serialization vectors form part of the implementation review. Stored payload and recomputed digest must match the referenced current record snapshot. No remote evidence fetch occurs during resolution.

## Scoped reads and current-fact consistency

The read port exposes only readiness(), loadFacts(lookup, transaction, now) and no generic query, write or list operation. lookup contains the authenticated actorId plus exact organizationId, branchId and capability. The resolver validates these before any persistence access. Each production call requires an explicit caller-owned ClientSession in an active snapshot transaction; no session-less fallback, nested transaction, unrelated session, cache, provider call or automatic retry. Missing/invalid session/readiness denies before authority reads. The adapter never starts/commits/ends the caller's transaction. It projects only required authority fields and returns plain immutable data to rules.

Exact Mongo query restrictions:

1. User: {_id: actorId, userType: 'user', isActive: true}; project ID/type/active only. This is an individual identity lookup, not a private patient/profile fetch.
2. Organization: {_id: organizationId, state: 'active', branches: {$elemMatch: {branchId, state: 'active'}}}; require exactly one matching embedded branch. A legacy business ID is read only after this mapping succeeds.
3. Pharmacy business: {_id: sourceBusinessId, isActive: true, isVerified: true, archivedAt: {$exists: false}}; project only ID/status and fingerprint source fields. Any present archivedAt, even malformed/null, denies under this strict new boundary. Unsupported kind denies before querying another business collection.
4. Membership: {organizationId, actorId, state: 'active', validFrom: {$lte: now}, expiresAt: {$gt: now}, grants: {$elemMatch: {branchId, capability}}}. Enforce one current row and one matching grant; ambiguity denies.
5. Professional eligibility: {organizationId, actorId, profession: requiredProfession, state: 'verified', validFrom: {$lte: now}, expiresAt: {$gt: now}}. Enforce one row and matching branch/capability in the verification decision.
6. Each decision: {_id: referencedDecisionId, organizationId, decisionKind: expectedKind, authorityGeneration: acceptedGeneration}; grant and professional decisions additionally require subjectActorId=actorId. Compare the full binding/digest in rules. Do not merge an externally supplied filter or use $or to relax these predicates.

Authority construction is the explicitly narrow bootstrap query boundary preceding a verified BusinessScope; it may inspect only the requesting person's authority in the exact requested organization. It is not a generic exception allowing other modules to read unscoped business or patient records. No list/count/aggregate/export/file/job surface is added in this slice. Future private business repositories must require the minted scope and compose restrictive ownership/branch predicates on every operation.

Capture one finite server time from an injected trusted clock per resolution, never a request timestamp; pass that exact value to loadFacts and rules. Require validFrom <= now < expiresAt for membership and professional eligibility, with finite dates and valid intervals. Require mapping/grant/verification decisions not in the future. Scope expiresAt is the earlier membership/eligibility expiry. Every invocation reloads facts in its transaction; no JWT role cache or cross-request reuse. Database errors, missing/duplicate rows, malformed facts, unknown evidence and readiness failure reject; no catch returns an allow result.

A successful result is a deeply frozen, internally minted BusinessScope containing actorId, organizationId, exactly one branchId, purpose=staff, capability, kind/sourceBusinessId, organization/branch/membership/eligibility revisions, exact decision/evidence references, checkedAt and expiresAt. Minting uses a module-private runtime identity check (for example, a WeakSet) rather than trusting a caller-shaped object or TypeScript brand alone. Do not include patient details, license contents, bearer tokens or unnecessary profile data. This is a reusable internal authority result, not a new session/JWT or proof of patient consent.

## Revocation, sensitive commands and audit boundary

The initial resolver establishes eligibility at its transaction snapshot. It does not promise that a later mutation or delivery is safe merely because a scope object exists. No sensitive command is activated in this slice. Before a prescription/report/financial/stock writer consumes this interface, its separate contract must resolve/revalidate in the command transaction, compare current subject/resource/document versions and perform a genuine shared write/CAS fence against concurrent authority revocation. Reading the same old snapshot twice is insufficient. Every grant/revoke and subject/business disable path participating in that contract must conflict on the same fences; until that is implemented and race-tested, sensitive command activation stays closed. Delayed jobs must resolve current authority afresh and preserve the initiator; a captured scope is not a durable grant.

Protected decision interfaces are data contracts here, not an approval/rejection endpoint. A future clinical writer binds the individual, scope and authority revisions to immutable patient/document/item/order versions, reason and decision time. It must distinguish imported/unverified evidence from finalized clinical authorship and enforce current patient/purpose authorization separately. This contract makes no prescription decision and releases no report. Finance/recovery permissions and stock-quality release require their own closed capabilities and contracts; do not reuse pharmacy.prescription.review for them.

No audit sink is invented or falsely claimed operational in this slice. The resolver returns a redacted decision reference set for the future protected command audit. It must not log raw tokens, credential documents, patient data or arbitrary record bodies. Public adapters added later must map missing authentication to 401, denied/hidden authority to one uniform 403 AUTHORITY_DENIED without tenant-existence details, and temporary readiness/mapping infrastructure failure to a generic unavailable response. Internally preserve typed denial categories for focused checks. An existing route is never silently changed by this work.

## Bootstrap, activation and indexes

The initial slice has no provisioning escape hatch. The readiness port defaults closed, records are not auto-created on login, and no existing admin/business/self-profile capability is trusted. A later independently reviewed local protected bootstrap/grant command must establish the first real organization mapping and branch, independently verify the individual and professional evidence, preserve a protected operation/evidence record, prove the issuer's authority without circular self-granting, and install/verify the required indexes through the create-only readiness process. It must distinguish developer-created synthetic fixtures from real grants and must not derive production authority from test data. Real professional verification and individual clinical decisions remain human workflow facts; no additional product-policy naming question is needed to develop this boundary.

Declared correctness indexes:

- Organization unique {kind:1, sourceBusinessId:1}.
- Membership unique {organizationId:1, actorId:1}, across every state; revoked rows are not deleted to permit a second conflicting current membership.
- Eligibility unique {organizationId:1, actorId:1, profession:1}, across every state.
- Decision unique {organizationId:1, operationId:1}; same operation with a different payload is a conflict, not a new decision. _id uniqueness also applies.

Do not rely on a schema declaration as proof of installed uniqueness. Readiness must verify exact keys/options, conflict-free data and supported transaction topology before real activation; no destructive syncIndexes/drop or background migration is admitted. Branch/grant uniqueness is explicit validation and future write-CAS responsibility, not a purported Mongo multikey uniqueness guarantee. No live records or users are provisioned by this contract.

## Verification and acceptance

Initial source-only acceptance requires two independent nonauthor implementation reviews, exact source/composition bindings, no unintended imports/wiring and explicit NOT_RUN runtime/index status. Pure-rule and read-port checks must exercise behavior, not merely match source strings. Execution needs a separately frozen launcher/source closure under current C3 rules; this document does not itself admit importing Mongoose, Node, the app or providers.

Required focused cases before claiming resolver runtime acceptance:

- Valid pharmacy person, active exact organization/branch, matching current grant/credential/evidence/generation and business fingerprint produces exactly one frozen scoped result; injected time boundaries are deterministic.
- Missing principal, each non-person token kind, inactive/missing User, malformed/castable IDs, missing/wrong purpose, unknown capability and altered requested actor fail before unauthorized reads.
- Two businesses and two branches reject cross-organization records, another subject's membership/credential/decision, mismatched decision kinds/revisions/digests/evidence and forged caller-shaped scope objects.
- Missing/false/unknown readiness, wrong generation, missing index proof, unsupported lab mapping, absent/changed source fingerprint and changed license fields deny; no fallback to legacy isVerified/Admin.permissions exists.
- Missing/duplicate/ambiguous membership/credential/grant/branch, suspended/revoked state, expired/future/invalid dates, future decisions, self-grant/self-verification and unknown schema/revision all deny.
- Adapter recording tests assert the actual restrictive predicates/projections and the exact same supplied transaction for every read; no unscoped lookup, arbitrary FilterQuery merge, provider access, writes or nested session occurs. Read/clock failures propagate, and returned objects cannot be mutated into a broader scope.
- Separately admitted replica-set/index checks prove installed constraints and snapshot consistency; later command checks prove revoke/disable vs approval races through real shared fences, replay/conflicting payload handling and protected audit atomicity. No future command is enabled based on pure or source-only passes.

Corporate, HR and hospital expansion and the final cross-module integration campaign remain deferred. C2 dependency/runtime/start conditions, C3 pre-import admission, focused clinical/financial/security evidence and application/release gates remain. This slice does not resolve F1; it supplies the shared authority prerequisite for its approval/recovery implementation.

# Individual-customer generic booking fields — implementation contract draft

12 November 2026. DRAFT ONLY. Author: internal Codex /root/booking_read_spec. Two actual independent NONAUTHOR Spec/Standards decisions on the exact draft/hash precede implementation; the author cannot approve this draft. Root owns source assignment, snapshot coordination and integration. This document alone authorizes no application edits or execution. Amendment 1 supersedes the rejected d45ca5c0 draft: SYSTEM_DESIGN AR-26 requires object/action authorization before forbidden-field422. The prior Root preliminary approval is superseded; both nonauthor contract reviews must be fresh. The exact old draft and compact REQUEST_CHANGES provenance are retained under output/qa/customer-booking-fields/contract-review-1/.

## Baseline, design and selected default

Focus worktree: /Users/shubham/Desktop/SwasthaDisha/SwasthaDisha-worktrees/customer-pharmacy-lab. Observed HEAD f89bec38be91a2ec63b15b2262a632aa32554f22; selected source bindings below are authoritative despite unrelated concurrent work. Booking controller remains c3b500d9343150d5edff79980f10825ce6592d02f1a1c7ea652f8c852c0ca76c. Preserve it and every other R5-selected source during capture. Root must resolve that snapshot dependency or explicitly authorize an isolated worktree before implementation. Do not silently refresh these pins.

Read with CUSTOMER_PHARMACY_LAB_GAPS, CUSTOMER_PHARMACY_LAB_EXECUTION, prior read/write-owner contracts, M0_A_PROGRESS, PARALLEL_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW and C2/C3. SYSTEM_DESIGN sections 4–6, 8.2 and AR-26 (line445) separate verified ownership, patient input, clinician authorship, money and controlled appointment transitions. AR-26 and USER_ROUTE_AUTHORITY_CONTRACT require forbidden-field422 only after object/action authorization; this slice chooses no exception. The existing create/reschedule DTOs already accept booking notes; prescription, report, follow-up and lifecycle are separate fields. The design does not give customers authority to assert those facts through a generic update.

The user delegated product/technical choices to Root. Select a conservative concrete default: an exact ordinary customer may replace only the existing free-text booking notes while the owned booking is pending or confirmed. Notes are request metadata, never a prescription, signed clinical note, proof of consent/payment, protected audit record or staff authority. No other generic PUT field is customer-editable in this slice. This deliberately excludes contact numbers/identity changes, concern/history amendments, supporting documents and address/mode changes pending their own authority/version/logistics contracts. No further owner naming question is required for this default. Real clinical/financial/privacy facts and release gates remain separate.

## Exact current behavior and why a separate narrow service path is needed

The graph discovers BookingController/BookingService in project swasthadisha but remains indexed against the original checkout at bfb608e; its inbound update trace returned no callers. Exact current files and the already verified specialist caller are authoritative, not graph absence.

- Authentication mounts before the bookings router. PUT /api/v1/bookings/:id runs params validation, shared update-body validation, query validation, then BookingController.update.
- The controller already resolves signed ownership using resolveBookingOwnerScope before ensureHRReadOnly and calls BookingService.update(id, body, owner). Reuse that helper unchanged; do not create another actor/owner resolver.
- UpdateBookingRequest and shared update Joi admit corporateId, slot/date/time/mode/address, documents, prescription, report, followUp, primaryConcern, consultationMode, contacts, status, paymentStatus, notes and cancellationReason. The internal DTO also contains lifecycle, cancelledAt and virtualMeeting; Joi does not directly admit those three.
- The shared validator uses abortEarly:false and stripUnknown:true, then replaces req.body. Unknown input is not a reliable raw-body rejection boundary. Existing invalid-field value errors occur before controller authorization.
- BookingService.update first performs getById(id, owner), then derives lifecycle/payment fields and writes with only {_id:id}. A notes-only call on an already cancelled booking still invokes ensureCancelledBookingPaymentStatus, which can mark payment refunded, then clears reminders/cancels meetings. A concurrent completion can also select completion/follow-up effects. An allowlist followed by this unchanged generic algorithm would not establish a notes-only mutation.
- SpecialistPortalService.updateAppointmentStatus calls the shared update without a customer owner. Preserve this signature and its behavior; do not globally restrict its DTO or shared Joi. Preserving it is not certification of specialist/admin/other-role authority.

## Bounded production scope

Only three existing production files may change:

1. src1/modules/bookings/controller/index.ts: select the new narrow service operation for exact userType=user after the unchanged owner resolver and HR readonly call. Pass the resolved signed owner, not query/body userId. All other well-shaped actors retain the existing BookingService.update call and arguments. Preserve success/error envelopes and every sibling handler/helper.
2. src1/modules/bookings/services/index.ts: add one updateCustomerNotes(id, data, signedOwner) operation containing the single authoritative customer field/type rule and restricted note write described below. It must not delegate to generic update or any business-effect helper. Leave the complete existing update method and its other callers unchanged.
3. src1/modules/bookings/types/index.ts: at most one narrow alias, CustomerBookingUpdateRequest = Required<Pick<UpdateBookingRequest, 'notes'>>, for the new operation. Do not duplicate the generic DTO or broaden it. Static typing complements, never replaces, the operation's runtime validation.

No route, shared Joi/validation middleware, repository/model, auth, contact, cancellation/reschedule/retry-payment/delete, payment/wallet/slot/queue/meeting, logger, root dependency/runtime/build/start or provider changes. No generic policy engine, middleware framework, new container dependency, duplicated ownership helper, copied controller archive or lexical-test framework. Source QA may record compact diff/hashes/reviews separately after authorization.

## Exact ordinary-customer rule and operation order

An ordinary customer is exact authenticated userType === 'user', using the signed _id unchanged. Ownership is not patient/dependent consent. The existing resolver supplies the owner and preserves its precedence:

1. Existing upstream JWT/params/body/query validation remains unchanged. Missing/expired/invalid JWT and existing 400 VALIDATION_ERROR outputs retain their present order/messages.
2. resolveBookingOwnerScope retains controller 401 UNAUTHORIZED / Authentication is required for malformed actor, then 403 FORBIDDEN / Access to bookings owned by another user is not permitted for a nonmatching supplied query owner. These happen before any booking service call. ensureHRReadOnly retains 403 FORBIDDEN / HR has view-only access to bookings for exact HR.
3. Exact customers dispatch once to updateCustomerNotes with the exact signed owner. Other actors dispatch once to unchanged generic update. No preliminary unscoped read or fallback is introduced.

Proposed performance gates remain those in [PERFORMANCE_PLAN.md](PERFORMANCE_PLAN.md): list/simple reads p95 <=500 ms; local transactional commands p95 <=1,000 ms; authenticated durable webhook acknowledgement p95 <=300 ms; unexpected failures <0.1%; zero integrity violations. Provider completion has a separate SLO. Proposed recovery objectives are RPO <=15 minutes and RTO <=2 hours, subject to budget/operations approval; they are not current guarantees.

## 5. Business tenancy, patient identity and access

Initial storage: shared Mongo database/collections, with mandatory `organizationId` on private business records and `branchId`/department/store where relevant. Do not add a meaningless tenant field to global reference data or mistake a global patient identity for shared clinical access. Clinical artifacts belong to their responsible organization plus explicit authorized care relationships.

Build staff request context from verified identity and active membership: `actorId`, actor kind, organization, allowed branches, role capabilities, assignments and purpose. A path/body/header organization is a requested scope; the server verifies membership before using it. Patient/caregiver principals instead carry verified patient relationships and purpose, without requiring business membership; the service resolves the target record's business and intersects patient rights with release/sharing policy. A dual-role user chooses the active purpose, never a union of patient and staff privileges. Deny by default. Scope lists, counts, detail, mutations, aggregates, exports, document grants and background jobs. Administrative cross-business access is a separate audited capability with reason and MFA; support has no routine full-record access. [OWASP object-level authorization](https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization/).

**Repository enforcement point.** Business-owned collections are accessible through a typed scoped repository/query gateway requiring verified `BusinessScope` (organization, permitted branches and actor/purpose). Methods cover ID reads, lists/counts, insert/upsert, update/delete, bulk and aggregation. They compose caller criteria with restrictive scope, reject caller-supplied ownership changes and deny an empty/invalid scope. Joins/lookups must scope each private collection and verify cross-record ownership; an arbitrary FilterQuery alone is not a security contract.

CI import/architecture rules prohibit direct business-model access outside approved scoped adapters and the explicit audited admin adapter. Runtime guards fail closed on missing scope and emit a redacted security event; merely alerting after an unscoped query is insufficient. Global reference collections are enumerated separately. The existing unscoped `BaseRepository` remains a legacy implementation until migrated: new business modules cannot use it directly, while M0 fixes existing caller ownership and migration wrappers before M1 extends the shared model. Two-business/branch fixtures exercise real list/detail/count/aggregate/export/file/jobs and write paths; static lint cannot prove arbitrary query correctness by itself.

| Actor | Normal access | Additional condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patient/caregiver | Verified own/represented care and bills | Explicit account-to-patient relationship; shared phone is insufficient |
| Reception/cashier | Branch registration, queue, permitted tariffs and receipts | No clinical signoff, unrestricted exports or refund override |
| Doctor | Assigned encounters/history needed for care, prescriptions and reviews | Author/finalization permissions and current sharing policy |
| Lab technician/signatory | Assigned orders/specimens; signatory approves reports | Technician cannot self-promote or release outside authorized scope |
| Pharmacy/store staff | Assigned store operations and minimum prescription context | Pharmacist release/stock adjustments require designated capabilities |
| Independent vendor | Assigned commercial/service records and permitted statements | No whole patient chart or another business's private prices |
| Integration worker | Narrow command/business scope | Persist initiator; re-evaluate revocable permissions for sensitive delayed actions |

Minimal patient identity may be global, but search results are limited to authorized local relationships or a verified patient-led linking flow. Do not expose cross-business identity existence through autocomplete. Clinical services need `patientId`; wholesale buyers/nonclinical customers can be businesses without patient identity. Payer and patient are separate references.

Consent records capture purpose, scope, version, representative, method/language, provenance and effective/withdrawal times. Authorization evaluates current restrictions, assignment and approved legal basis; a blanket consent boolean or marketplace listing is insufficient. Withdrawal blocks future optional sharing/sends while historical record retention follows approved policy. Emergency access, minor/guardian rules, retention/legal holds and cross-business sharing require clinical/privacy signoff before enabling those paths.

CASL is a candidate policy library, not a tenancy guarantee. Revocation updates membership version; sensitive commands check current membership rather than trusting long-lived token roles. Keep existing authentication behind a strengthened interface; no fallback production JWT secret, fixed OTP bypass or unrestricted diagnostic/admin endpoints. Public listing off preserves accepted obligations and private workspace access.

## 7. Transactions, concurrency and idempotency

Mongo is the initial authoritative transactional store. Multi-document transactions require the supported replica-set/sharded deployment and configured durability; existing inventory already depends on sessions. Use short transactions with appropriate majority durability/read concerns verified against the selected server/driver. Bound retry of transient/unknown-commit outcomes and consult the command result before replaying effects. [MongoDB transactions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions/).

Every financial/stock/capacity-changing command needs a scoped idempotency key and normalized request hash. In one transaction, establish the unique command record, check actor/resource version and expected state, change owned records, append audit/effects and outbox, and persist the command result/reference. Concurrent duplicate keys resolve to the committed original result; a different body returns 409. Never leave a permanently unowned processing key: use transaction atomicity or a recoverable lease. Authentication/authorization precede returning any stored response.

| Command | Local atomic boundary | External work / compensation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Place pharmacy order | Order + explicit lot reservation + effect/audit/outbox + command result | Create gateway intent after commit; failure releases through a guarded command |
| Counter cash dispense | Approved prescription/price + order/invoice + receipt/journal + stock movement, if bounded | No gateway call; print/send after commit. Large bulk sale uses bounded drafts before final commit |
| Appointment hold | Conditional capacity increment + hold/appointment + outbox/result | Payment intent afterward; expiry/cancellation releases once |
| Apply verified collection | Unique capture effect + receipt/journal + allowed local booking/order transition | External fulfilment queued; failure enters recovery/refund policy |
| Finalize report | Expected draft version/signatory + release pointer + audit + review task/outbox | Notifications/webhooks after commit, only for approved recipients |
| Receive purchase/transfer | Remaining receivable check + lot balance + immutable movement + receipt state | Supplier payment/account export separately owned |
| Wallet reserve/capture/release | Guard selected account/pocket available funds and hold version; update posted/held counters, hold/movement, booking state and outbox/result together | External call facts are reconciled before expiry/capture; release and capture are mutually exclusive for the same amount |
| Refund completion | Confirmed provider result + unique refund effect/journal + refund state | Stock return and credit note remain explicit linked commands |

**M0 wallet mutation boundary (AR-14).** Every live customer-wallet debit/credit/refund uses one owned application operation and Mongo session: establish the unique economic effect key, conditionally update the authoritative balance with `$inc` (debit predicate requires available funds: posted minus held >= debit, within the selected currency/account and permitted purpose), insert the movement/transaction row, update dependent local booking/payment state and append outbox/result atomically. Duplicate effect keys return the committed original result; a crash rolls back both balance and movement. Partial wallet funding is selected under that transaction and snapshotted into the payment intent; a retry cannot deduct again or silently change a live gateway amount. [MongoDB atomic updates](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/write-operations-atomicity/).

Target wallet commands include reserve, capture and release as explicit idempotent operations. Authoritative posted/held counters share a guarded account/pocket document; available = posted - held and posted >= held >= 0. Reserving raises held only when available covers the amount; capture reduces posted and held once; release reduces held once. Ordinary debit/transfer and competing app/phone holds check that same available counter, not a snapshot sum of hold rows. Preserve any proven active holds in migration. Legacy held=0 is allowed only after confirming none exist; the new F14 hold workflow is not a new M0 dependency, but cannot launch until all affected debit paths enforce this contract.

M0 compatibility preserves an explicit balance-unit/currency contract; never increment a legacy rupee balance with unlabelled paise or silently change an existing gateway split. The normalized minor-unit cutover follows the reviewed pre-M2 migration. Replace the seven inspected read/insert/absolute-balance-update paths in bookings, externalBookings, payment recharge/refund and wallet services. The existing atomic credit and pharmacy-wallet guarded-debit helpers are useful primitives, but `$inc` alone does not atomically bind the ledger or suppress duplicates. Remove absolute read-modify-set balance mutations from normal flows; controlled initial creation and reviewed opening-balance cutover are separate initialization operations. Cover every reference type, not only the existing pharmacy-order refund partial index. Use operation identity for legitimate partial refunds and enforce the remaining refundable amount; do not wrongly deduplicate all partial refunds into one booking-wide key.

F13 verifies the wallet-effect uniqueness manifest and existing pharmacy+medicine unique index before affected mutations are enabled. Resolve duplicate/missing legacy evidence explicitly; never delete conflicting financial history to make an index build succeed. Mandatory tests: two wallet-funded bookings against funds for one; duplicate refunds; legitimate distinct partial refunds; crash between balance and movement writes; missing-index refusal. These are unexecuted release gates.

Use compare-and-set on state/version and conditional quantity/capacity predicates; application read-then-write checks alone are insufficient. If several FEFO lots are needed, deterministic selection and guarded decrements occur within the same bounded transaction. On contention retry selection; reject shortages without partial allocation. Available units = eligible on-hand minus reserved, excluding quarantined/expired stock.

Holds/reservations have explicit expiresAt, active/reconciling/capture-pending/consumed/released state and allocation records. Expiry and confirm race through guarded versions; only one wins. An open payment requires the bounded gateway-reconciliation protocol in section 9 before final release; the network call occurs outside the transaction while a fenced reconciling claim protects capacity. Commands reject an expired hold unless that explicit payment decision preserves it; delayed cleanup alone never extends a hold. Never delete live reservation/hold documents with TTL: capacity/stock release and audit must commit first. TTL is only later cleanup under retention policy; MongoDB does not promise immediate expiry deletion. [TTL behavior](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-ttl/).

### 8.1 Pharmacy and connected counter

Order: draft -> reserved -> accepted -> dispensing -> fulfilled; cancellation/expiry/partial fulfilment are explicit branches. Prescription verification/rejection and payment status are separate gates. Postpaid/cash policy may permit dispensing before a collection only for an authorized business configuration; it creates receivable, not a fictitious paid receipt.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Counter or app
  participant A as API PaymentIntentCoordinator
  participant D as Mongo transaction
  participant W as Recovery worker
  participant G as Payment gateway
  C->>A: Place order with idempotency key
  A->>D: Commit price, order, FEFO hold and creating payment intent
  D-->>A: Durable business and receipt references
  A->>G: Create gateway order outside transaction
  G-->>A: External reference or unknown timeout
  A->>D: Persist reference or recoverable unknown
  A-->>C: Checkout details or explicit processing result
  G->>A: Authenticated payment event
  A->>D: Durable inbox; captured fact required for collection
  W->>D: Apply money and guarded hold/recovery decision once
  C->>A: Authorized dispense command
  A->>D: Check prescription/payment policy and consume held lots
```

Retail/wholesale is price entitlement, not a duplicate stock pool. Snapshot approved buyer eligibility, tariff/rule version, minimum quantities, tax and UOM; do not trust client-calculated totals. An authorized counter price override is supported: staff capability, actor, reason, original/approved unit price, limit/approval policy and timestamp are recorded; the server recomputes totals/tax and snapshots the override. Existing unrestricted input is a gap to harden, not a requirement to remove all overrides. Partial fulfilment adjusts charge/refund and quantities explicitly. Customer returns reference original lines/lots and quantities already returned; inspect and quarantine where required before making stock saleable. Expired/recalled stock cannot re-enter usable inventory through a generic increment helper. Expiry is evaluated using the store's configured local date and approved manufacturer expiry precision/cutoff, not UTC `today`. The existing UTC YYYYMMDD comparison can retain stock after the intended local cutoff (up to 5h30 for Asia/Kolkata under end-of-local-day policy); test the boundary, month/date precision and every reserve/consume/release/list path. Unknown expiry is quarantined/reviewed, never fabricated.

Supplies use the same purchasing/location/movement principles but different item/service rules. A lab procedure consumes actual approved reagents once using a service-use key; record waste/overrides and reversals. A BOM is a proposal until staff confirms use. Included consumables do not produce a second customer charge. Transfers move source -> in-transit -> destination; destination rejects/shortfalls remain visible. Stock counts create authorized variances, not rewritten movement history.

**AR-27 quality transitions.** Receipt, count, adjustment, import, cancel, release and return preserve recalled, quarantined, expired or other quality holds regardless of positive quantity. Availability/depletion and quality approval are separate decisions. Only a separately authorized, version-checked quality-release command with evidence may change a releasable hold; manufacturer expiry/recall policy cannot be bypassed by quantity authorization. Use the current representation safely in M0; define any two-axis schema and historical mapping before M3.

**AR-32 lot price and quote contract.** For applicable medicines/packaged goods, validate the tax-inclusive allocated-unit charge against the applicable label/lot MRP and any lower verified current price-list/controlled limit, using exact pack-to-selling-unit conversion. Never add tax twice or use the latest item's display price as every FEFO lot's authority. Discounts, slabs and overrides cannot defeat that ceiling. Missing/ambiguous lot price/unit evidence requires approved review or safe refusal, not an invented unlimited cap. Preserve original sold terms on returns. Repricing a customer-originated placed order needs a new quote version and customer confirmation; an authorized counter override retains actor/reason/limits and is not general permission to rewrite a paid order. Finance/pharmacist/legal owners approve current applicability, source updates and units before the affected pricing release; this is not a legal certification. The Ministry describes inclusive MRP and the lower label/current-price-list constraint; later amendments and SKU/jurisdiction applicability still need owner review. [Official medicine pricing explanation](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1983964&lang=2&reg=3).

```mermaid
  D-->>C: Authorized report-ready event and review work
```

Fulfilment mode is snapshotted per assignment, not inferred from whether a lab later adds an API. Handing an order between modes requires an authorized handover, paused old writer, version increment, reconciled provider order and clear report provenance. Do not create a duplicate commercial order or let both modes finalize the same report. An API-delivered report still needs an established lab approval contract; do not blindly mark any uploaded PDF clinically verified. Use separate axes: acquisition `received`; completeness `preliminary|final|unknown`; approval/publication `draft|verified|released|rejected|superseded`. An amendment creates a new version linked by `amendsVersionId`, rather than modifying final bytes. A permitted preliminary release is conspicuously labelled with provider provenance/pending scope and does not imply all tests are final. Lab/clinical/privacy owners decide preliminary release and correction-notice policy before the pilot.

Every semantically new fetch/upload uses an immutable organization/order/version-scoped object key plus content hash and a version manifest. A hash is not a public lookup key or authorization. Duplicate callbacks with identical bytes, stage and provenance record delivery evidence without creating another clinical version; changed completeness/status can create a new version even with identical bytes. Release conditionally moves the current pointer and reopens/links clinician review; past review remains tied to its exact version. Corrections notify only currently permitted recipients through approved care/legal-basis rules, with ordering-clinician escalation where allowed; never silently add recipients after consent withdrawal. M0 stops stable-name overwrite and public cache use; legacy files retain `versionHistory: unknown` when prior bytes cannot be recovered.

**AR-35 existing provider fulfilment recovery.** Persist one scoped fulfilment intent/result for the local obligation and assigned provider before create. Concurrent client verification, worker and webhook paths cannot independently place the same provider order. Use provider-supported idempotency/reference lookup and account/integration-scoped external IDs; where capability is absent, retain pending/manual reconciliation rather than blind retry. Treat network reset, timeout and ambiguous 5xx as unknown until evidence resolves them. Preserve existing confirmation-pending behavior already present in some paths; do not claim that every timeout currently refunds. A local timer or cancellation request does not prove provider failure/cancellation or justify a completed refund. Refund obligations, actual returns and provider cancellation are distinct, with the shared captured-source budget. Authorized manual resolution requires reason/evidence and cannot bypass that budget. M0 covers the existing lab-payment fulfilment/recovery implementation; API-to-panel expansion remains M4. | Failure / race | Required behavior | Detection / recovery owner |

| Client times out after local commit | Same command key retrieves original authorized result | API/command metrics; backend |
| Capture after hold expiry | Preserve collection; controlled reallocation or refund/recovery | Payment reconciliation and oldest pending-compensation alert; finance/backend |

Logs use request/correlation/operation/event/resource IDs and safe status codes; redact tokens, identifiers beyond need, medical content and raw signatures. Metrics use bounded cardinality rather than patient IDs. Clinical access and privileged changes have protected audit records with actor, purpose, scope, before/after references and outcome; regular business users cannot edit them. Retention and access are separate from application debug logs.

Initial alert proposals: urgent if capture/refund discrepancies appear, unauthorized access occurs, accepted writes cannot reconcile or durable acceptance fails; warn if normal-task p95 age exceeds 30 seconds or backlog grows across successive windows. Clinical urgent-result escalation deadlines are set by the clinical team, not the normal queue SLO. Dashboards separate local API latency, provider completion, money recovery, sample/report turnaround, restore status and store/capacity reconciliation. Each alert/runbook has an accountable human role and replay/correction steps.

Backups encrypt database and object versions with independently protected keys. Restore into an isolated environment and reconcile patient mappings, report hashes, invoice/journal/stock totals, in-flight holds and pending events. After restore, re-pull gateway payment/order/refund and lab-provider facts across an overlapping recovery window from the restore point, compare existing external IDs and captured versions, and queue mismatches without duplicate effects. Source systems may contain newer captures/reports than the backup. Backup success alone does not prove RPO/RTO. Export supports authorized business continuity without exposing another business or silently losing amendments/financial references.

### 15.1 Restore admission and authority freshness (AR-29)

Keep sensitive access, optional sends and irreversible mutations closed while restoring. Advance a recovery generation in a protected control plane outside the restored rollback domain and require all API/worker instances to observe it before admission. Invalidate pre-restore sessions/access grants and all outstanding OTP/setup/reset challenges; do not restore usable consumed challenges. A new token minted after restore is not proof that restored membership, consent, caregiver, contact or credential data is current. Recover post-backup revocation/consumption evidence from an independently recoverable journal or require approved independent re-verification before issuing fresh authority. If freshness cannot be established, keep that subject/scope blocked with an accountable assisted route. Resume sensitive deliveries only after current recipient/purpose/authority is established; regenerated jobs do not inherit stale grants. Select the concrete control-plane/evidence mechanism and failure policy before restore acceptance; no additional microservice or external product is chosen here.
